thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple nodes in inference-gpu-pool reporting NotReady & kubelet restarts (cluster: prod-us-west-2). Auto-escalating to oncall.
olga: Seeing spike in 5xx from /v1/generate, dashboards show CPU steady but GPU nodes dropping out of ready state. ETA?

simon: I can take first pass. Which pools affected?

leah: inference-gpu-pool-1 and inference-gpu-pool-2. Started ~T-6m. ASG still has nodes but pods stuck Pending/ContainerCreating.

olga: Logs from the node show repeated kubelet restarts and 'failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime' errors. Full excerpt: ```May 12 03:02:14 ip-10-0-3-21 kubelet[1234]: E05012 03:02:14 kubelet.go:2021] Failed to start container "pod-xyz": runtime create failed: container_linux.go:xxx: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:xxx: exec: "device error": unknown
```

simon: That looks like driver / kernel flake with containerd ramp. Can you paste `kubectl describe node` for one of the NotReady nodes?

olga: Pasting relevant bits: ```Conditions: Ready=False (KubeletNotReady) Kubelet has restarted 4 times in last 5m
Non-terminated Pods: 22 (20 infra, 2 system) Allocatable: gpu:1 GPU driver: Unknown```

infra-runner: I've kicked a runbook check: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/node-kubelet-restarts - steps 1-3 in progress.

leah: Customer impact: error rate for hosted inference up from baseline 0.3% to 6.8%, p95 latency doubled for some routes. Some tenants hit failover to Dedicated.

simon: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Cordon affected nodes, 2) Scale up warm spare pool, 3) Reroute traffic off pool via routing-policy fallback, 4) Try soft-restart of kubelet on one node to validate kernel/driver state.

olga: Cordon done for ip-10-0-3-21 and ip-10-0-3-45 (`kubectl cordon <node>`). Pods are getting rescheduled but backpressure on other nodes.

oncall-bot: Note: automated routing fallback engaged for customers on standard tier. Dedicated customers are unaffected.

simon: Scaling warm spares by +3 now (`terraform apply -var=pool_size=8`), monitoring new node joins.

leah: I've posted an incident banner to status page: "Degraded: Inference responses may return 5xx or increased latency for some hosted customers." Linking to incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1999999999

infra-runner: Trying soft-restart on ip-10-0-3-21: `ssh ec2-user@ip-10-0-3-21 sudo systemctl restart kubelet && sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager`

olga: After restart, node came back Ready for ~90s then dropped again. Journal shows GPU driver crashes preceding kubelet restart: `nvidia: GPU hung, recovery failed` 

simon: That confirms GPU driver/kernel instability. Next step: drain node and remove from rotation, mark for full host reboot and kernel rollback candidate. Drain and evict pods gracefully.

olga: Draining ip-10-0-3-21: `kubectl drain ip-10-0-3-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> some pods pending due to scarce GPU alloc. Rescheduling onto warm spares in progress.

leah: Allocations: warm spares have enough capacity, tail latencies now trending down but errors still present from older requests in queue.

simon: I'm going to update fleet autoscaling policy to bring another +2 nodes and mark 2 nodes for health check reboots. Doing now.

infra-runner: Marked nodes ip-10-0-3-21 and ip-10-0-3-45 as EVACUATE, added instance tag `reboot-required=true` for infra team to handle.

olga: Paging infra oncall (pager: @infra-team) to coordinate host-level reboots and driver checks. @inf-team please validate driver version and any recent AMI changes.

(reacts: incident-bot :eyes:)

infra-runner: Infra confirmed a recent kernel patch rolled to the AMI in last deploy window. Rolling AMI rollback candidate and validating new boots in staging.

simon: For customer communication: Leah, please prepare a short note that we are mitigating GPU driver/kernel issue causing node flaps and that dedicated customers unaffected. Include ETA ~30-60m for full recovery.

leah: Drafted: "We are investigating an infrastructure issue causing GPU hosts to restart unexpectedly, impacting hosted inference. Engineers are draining affected hosts and scaling capacity. Some requests may receive 5xx errors or increased latency. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Posting now.

olga: Observability: added temporary alert threshold for unhealthy nodes to reduce noise: `node.kubelet.restarts > 2m` -> notify only sev2+ 

simon: Handoff: My shift ends in 40m. If this persists past that, will hand off to @olga for follow-up. Key action items for next oncall: 1) Confirm infra rebooted hosts and driver version, 2) remove `reboot-required` tags when complete, 3) verify no further kubelet restarts for 15m, 4) rollback routing fallback when stable.

olga: Acknowledged. I'll take post-shift ownership if still open.

oncall-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2 (user-facing errors, partial degradation).

infra-runner: Infra done rebooting ip-10-0-3-21 with rolled-back AMI; driver appears stable on boot. Running soak checks.

leah: Error rate down to 1.2%, p95 returning toward baseline. Removing status page auto-update note to indicate improving.

simon: Thanks team. Leaving a brief postmortem note in #postmortems link: https://wiki.internal/redwood/incidents/1999999999-brief with timeline and actions.

olga: Final checks: holding for 20m soak. If no recurrence, I'll uncordon and bring nodes back into pool one by one.

infra-runner: Soak passed 22m on ip-10-0-3-21, driver stable. Uncordon candidate scheduled.

olga: Uncordoned ip-10-0-3-21. Pods scheduling fine. Monitoring.

leah: Status page updated to "Investigating -> Partial mitigation" -> will move to "Resolved" when all nodes stable and p95 < 1.2x baseline.

simon: Closing note before handoff: Root cause likely a rolling AMI/kernel update with a regressed GPU driver interaction. Action items: 1) pin kernel-driver combo in AMI builds, 2) add pre-deploy GPU driver health checks to bakery pipeline, 3) create automated host reboot playbook.

olga: Taking over post-shift. Thanks all.
